topic: Strategy and risk in overseas expansion
question: Tanvir Textiles Ltd, a fictional mid-sized garment exporter from Tiruppur, earns most of its revenue from one European buyer. To cut costs and get closer to customers, the board is considering setting up a factory in another Asian country with lower wages. As a strategy consultant, discuss the strategic and risk factors the board should evaluate before deciding.
sources: Generally accepted strategic management frameworks (PESTLE, SWOT, Porter's five forces)
Generally accepted enterprise risk management principles (for example the COSO ERM Framework, 2017)

points.label: Strategic fit and customer concentration
points.description: Whether the move fits the long-term strategy, and the high dependence on one buyer, which the expansion should reduce rather than increase.
points.basis: Strategic management: strategic fit and customer dependence

points.label: Country and political risk
points.description: Political stability, labour laws, taxation, trade agreements, rules on repatriating profits and ease of doing business in the host country.
points.basis: Strategic management: PESTLE analysis of the host country

points.label: Cost and financial evaluation
points.description: Whether lower wages survive after productivity, logistics, set-up costs and duties; project appraisal of cash flows and funding, and currency risk on investment and earnings.
points.basis: Corporate finance: international capital budgeting and exchange risk

points.label: Entry mode and operations
points.description: Choice between own factory, joint venture or contract manufacturing; supply chain, quality control, management capacity and buyer compliance standards.

points.label: Risk response and governance
points.description: A risk register with mitigation (hedging, insurance, phased investment, diversifying buyers) and board monitoring of the project against agreed milestones.
points.basis: COSO ERM Framework: risk response and monitoring
